title: Tests and quality gates
tagline: How every change is checked offline: pytest guard rails, test data, layer rules
summary: About 3,800 pytest tests check the whole stack without the game: on made-up maps and frames, saved game frames, cuts of live telemetry and the offline simulator. A shared conftest makes every test offline and deterministic, a small module finds the big labelled frame sets that live outside git, and a code-reading test enforces the layer rules and keeps the elevated key player lean. Golden traces and harness tables sit beside the suite as the next gates.
details_md:
The suite is plain pytest over `tests/`: 145 `test_*.py` files and 3,818 collected tests on 2026-11-16, 64 of them marked `slow`. `python -m pytest` runs the rest on 8 pytest-xdist workers (pytest-xdist is the plugin that spreads tests over parallel worker processes) in about a minute (README.md); `python -m pytest --slow` runs everything, about 3 minutes, and is what the top-level README.md asks for before a commit. Nothing in the suite needs the game: no test may press a key, look at the screen or write into the live lab (`gamelab/lab`, the git-ignored folder of learned models, logs, recordings and the notes the running processes leave each other).

**Three layers of protection.** First, `tests/conftest.py` sets environment variables at import, before gamelab loads: her stats as measured (`GAMELAB_FIXED_STATS`), the thief as the character, one OpenBLAS thread, the GPU off and no phone pushes. Second, its autouse `offline` fixture (autouse: pytest wraps every test in it without the test asking) refuses or redirects, for each test, every way out of the process the code knows of: key sends, window calls, screen capture (DXGI desktop duplication, Windows' screen-copy API, and the `mss` screenshot library), plans to the key player (the separate administrator process that presses the keys), paging the phone, starting the perception service, and every lab note (alarm, guard, stop, touches, stats, damage), plus a write guard on `gamelab/lab`. Third, simulator runs put their own fakes in place (`gamelab/sim/fakes.py`'s `patched`: fake clock, fake player, lab paths moved to a temp folder) and raise `SimViolation` if anything slips past.

**Three kinds of test data.**

- Small fixtures in git: `tests/fixtures` (235 files, about 36 MB): crops and frames of the game (capture, heading, touches, misses, deaths, the Lie Detector, Violetta), label files, and JSON cut from live telemetry and logs (e.g. `hunt_stays_2026-11-05.json`, `regular_live_2026-10-28.json`). Six folders carry a README saying where each frame came from.
- Big labelled frame sets outside git, found by `tests/testdata.py` in `gamelab/lab/testdata` (or `GAMELAB_TESTDATA`). A missing set makes its tests fail, not skip, unless `GAMELAB_NO_TESTDATA=1`.
- The game's own data (`gamedata/data`, not in git): real-map tests, including every simulator scenario on Tree Dungeon, skip without it.

**Code-reading gates.** Several tests read the source rather than run it: `test_architecture.py` (layer imports, the elevated player's imports, one capturing process), `test_rate.py` (one perception rate, no other frames-a-second constant), `test_geometry.py` (nothing but the simulator assumes the 1920x1080 window), `test_testdata.py` (no test reads frames from a scratch folder or a pruned lab folder) and `test_review_pages.py` (no path tied to one PC).

**The simulator in the suite.** `test_sim.py` runs every registered scenario and checks it shows what it's there for (`scenarios.unmet` empty), that runs are deterministic, and that a trip stepped as the hunt loop drives it gives the same trace. Many other files (test_harness, test_retreat, test_statcheck, test_target...) build small worlds or frozen scenes on Tree Dungeon's data. The golden traces, the exact record of what every scenario did (its key plans, log lines and results), are checked outside pytest with `python -m gamelab.sim.golden check`.

**Shared helpers.** `tests/` has no `__init__.py`, so pytest puts it on `sys.path` and test files import each other's helpers: test_sim's made-up map (`tree`, `model`, `plat`, `KEYS`, `tap`, `still`), test_worldstate's `small_map` and `Drawn` eyes, test_danger's `build` and `HER`, test_attack's `PLAT`, `target` and `step_map`, test_navigation's `tree` and `by_y`, test_pasted's `frame` and `FRAMES`, test_fight's `EMPTY_MAP`, `_Eyes` and `hunter`, test_alarm's fake game. Besides `testdata.py` there is no separate helpers module.

**The order to check a change** (gamelab/README.md, from 2026-10-28): targeted tests while working and the fast suite before a commit (the top-level README.md asks for `--slow` there: the two disagree); the goldens of the map worked on, on a pool (`golden check NAMES --jobs 2`); the smallest harness table that answers the question against master's cached baseline (`harness ab`); for a perception change, her recordings replayed and scored (`sim.replay`); and a reviewer's spot checks of the author's seeds.

modules.title: The suite's guard rails (conftest)
modules.tagline: Makes every test offline, deterministic and harmless; runs the suite on 8 workers
modules.summary: pytest loads this file before any test. At import it fixes the environment (her measured stats, one OpenBLAS thread, GPU off, no phone pushes) before anything imports gamelab. Its hooks add `--slow`, pick the number of xdist workers and leave the slow tests out by default. Its autouse `offline` fixture stops every test from pressing a key, touching the game window, capturing the screen, sending a plan to the player, paging anyone or writing under the real `gamelab/lab`.
modules.details_md:
**At import, before gamelab loads.** Five environment settings come first because gamelab reads them once, when it's first imported:

- `GAMELAB_FIXED_STATS=1`: `motion.physics` works out her walk and jumps from her stats once at import. With this set it takes the measured defaults (`physics.FIXED_STATS`), not `config.toml`'s `[character]`. Before it (2026-10-20), setting SPEED 125 in the file failed 16 tests and changed every golden trace.
- `GAMELAB_CHARACTER` is removed: the tests play the thief, whoever the shell names.
- `OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1` (unless set): with OpenBLAS's 24 threads a bare `import numpy` committed about 3 GB a process.
- `GAMELAB_GPU=0` (unless set): the re-finds' GPU path stays off unless a test turns it on.
- `GAMELAB_NO_PUSH=1`: `control.notify` never reads the lab's own push and mail files. On 2026-10-29 ~05:35 the suite in the main checkout texted the user a Lie Detector alert from a test's fake screen.

**Hooks.** `pytest_addoption` adds `--slow`. `pytest_collection_modifyitems` deselects every item marked `slow` unless `--slow` is given (they are reported as deselected, not skipped). `pytest_xdist_auto_num_workers` answers pyproject's `-n auto`: 0 workers (one process) when every command-line argument is a file or a test inside one, since a worker takes about 4 s to start; otherwise 8, not one per core, because each worker commits about half a GB. pyproject.toml adds `--dist worksteal` (long tests handed to workers as they come free) and `-rfEs` (the summary lists failures, errors and every skip with its reason).

**`offline` (autouse, every test).** It uses `monkeypatch` (pytest's fixture that replaces an attribute for one test and puts the original back afterwards), so everything is undone after the test, and a test that needs one of these replaces it with its own fake later, which wins. A refused call raises `AssertionError("<name> called in a test")`.

- Keys and windows: `maplehelper.win32.send_key` and `foreground_title`; 15 functions of `gamelab.window` (`bring_to_front`, `move_cursor`, `find_game`, `client_rect`, ...).
- Capture: `capture.Dxgi` (desktop duplication) and `capture._open_mss` refused; `capture._SHARED` cleared so no grabber outlives its test.
- The key player: `client.INBOX` / `OUTBOX` moved into the test's `tmp_path`; the Lie Detector alarm file (`ALARM`) moved in `paths`, `alarm`, `client` and `player`; `alarm.page` refused.
- Lab notes: `paths.VITALS`, `HUNT`, `STOP_HUNT`, `PARK_NOTE`, `PARKED`, `GUARD`, `GUARD_MODE`, `TOUCHES`, `STATS`, `STAT_WINDOW`, `STAT_TEMPLATES`, `DAMAGE` (and `Files.damage`) all moved to `tmp_path`; `guard.LOOP_STOP` too (the grind-loop scripts' stop file, outside the lab at `D:/MapleHelper-scratch/mageq/empty/STOP`, so the write guard below would not catch it); `character.CHOSEN` to `tmp_path/character.json` and `character._ACTIVE` copied so who plays is the test's own.
- Processes and mutexes: `service._start_detached` refused (no perception service started); the window-size fix's `WINDOW_TRIES` file and `LOCK` mutex, and the rolling recorder's `MUTEX`, renamed per process id and `tmp_path` so parallel workers never share one.
- `damage.THREADED = False`: her damage fits run at once, the same every run.
- `locate.build` wrapped by `_own_lab`: a lab folder under the live lab becomes the same folder under `tmp_path/lab` (2026-11-03: 7 tests failed only in the main checkout because the live lab had her plate model and Tree Dungeon's art cached).
- Finally `sim.fakes._write_guards(paths.LAB)`: `open`, `io.open`, `os.open` in a write mode, and `os.replace`, `rename`, `remove`, `unlink`, `mkdir`, `rmdir`, `utime` raise `SimViolation` for any path under `gamelab/lab`. Reading the lab stays allowed.

**`her_profile_speed` (autouse).** After each test it calls `motion.physics.reset()`, putting her planner's walk and climb back to her profile's SPEED, so a test that set another (`physics.set_speed`, a hunter that read her stat window) doesn't leak it into the next.

**`config_data`.** A deep copy of `BASE_CONFIG`, a fixed stand-in for `config.toml`, so editing her real keys never breaks a test. Used by `test_config`, `test_controller` and `test_character`.

key_items.name: offline
key_items.summary: Runs around every test: refuses keys, windows, screen capture and paging, moves every lab file a test could touch into its tmp_path, and installs the write guard on gamelab/lab.
key_items.details_md: Refusals raise `AssertionError("<what> called in a test")`. Redirections cover the inbox and outbox (plans go nowhere a player looks), the alarm file in four modules (a lab copied while the alarm was up once had every test plan refused, 2026-10-24), the guard's and stop's notes, her touches, stats, stat window calibration and damage, and who plays. Named mutexes get `-test-<pid>-<tmp_path.name>` suffixes.

key_items.name: pytest_xdist_auto_num_workers
key_items.summary: How many xdist workers `-n auto` means: 0 when the run names only files or tests, else 8.
key_items.details_md: `all(Path(arg.split('::')[0]).is_file() for arg in config.args)`. A folder or the whole suite gets 8; `-n 8` or `-n 0` on the command line says it outright.

key_items.name: pytest_collection_modifyitems
key_items.summary: Without `--slow`, removes every item marked `slow` and reports them as deselected.
key_items.details_md: On 2026-11-16 that's 64 of 3,818 collected tests (test_no_hit_scenes 23, test_sim 20, test_probe 13, test_retreat 3, test_stat_window 2, test_records, test_replay and test_sim_magic 1 each).

key_items.name: pytest_addoption
key_items.summary: Adds the `--slow` flag: also run the tests marked slow, for before a commit.

key_items.name: GAMELAB_FIXED_STATS
key_items.summary: Her stats as measured, not config.toml's, set before anything imports gamelab.
key_items.details_md: The goldens and the harness restart themselves with the same setting, so tests, traces and harness tables all plan with the same walk and jumps.

key_items.name: GAMELAB_NO_PUSH
key_items.summary: No Lie Detector push or text from the lab's own Bark and mail files (control.notify.NO_PUSH_ENV).

key_items.name: OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS
key_items.summary: One OpenBLAS thread, so each worker doesn't commit about 3 GB when numpy loads.

key_items.name: GAMELAB_GPU
key_items.summary: The re-finds' GPU matching off unless a test turns it on, whatever the lab's GPU file says.

key_items.name: BASE_CONFIG
key_items.summary: A fixed stand-in for config.toml: window title, keys, hotkeys, control keys and the throw gap.

key_items.name: config_data
key_items.summary: A fresh deep copy of BASE_CONFIG for a test to edit.

key_items.name: _own_lab
key_items.summary: Wraps localization.locate.build so a lab folder under the live lab is read from the test's own lab instead.
key_items.details_md: Paths are compared with `os.path.normcase(os.path.abspath(...))`; anything equal to or under `live` is rebased onto `own` with `os.path.relpath`. Tests that want a locator save the models in their own folder and are untouched.

key_items.name: her_profile_speed
key_items.summary: After every test, `physics.reset()` puts her walk and climb back to her profile's SPEED.

gotchas: The environment lines only work because conftest is imported before any test imports gamelab; setting GAMELAB_FIXED_STATS later in a test changes nothing already computed.

Names imported by value (`from ..paths import ALARM`) are copies, so the fixture patches each module holding one (ALARM in paths, alarm, client and player). A new module that imports a lab path by name isn't redirected unless added here; the write guard is the backstop.
The write guard raises `SimViolation` with the simulator's wording ("during a simulated run") even in a plain test.
Running one file or test uses no workers; pass `-n 8` to spread it anyway.
Slow tests are deselected, not skipped, so they don't appear in the `-rfEs` skip list.
Only `gamelab/lab` has the write guard: a file elsewhere (like `guard.LOOP_STOP` in the scratch folder) is safe only because `offline` redirects it by name.

modules.title: Test data outside git
modules.tagline: Finds big labelled frame sets outside git; a missing set fails loudly, never silently
modules.summary: Saved game frames too big for git live in `gamelab/lab/testdata/<set>`, their hand-made labels in `tests/fixtures`. This module lists the sets, finds them (an environment variable, this checkout, then the main checkout of a git worktree), and makes a test whose set is missing fail saying where it looked. `GAMELAB_NO_TESTDATA=1` turns those failures into skips, and a set known to be lost skips with "NEEDS A NEW CAPTURE".
modules.details_md:
**Why it exists.** Until 2026-10-28 tests read labelled frames from `D:/MapleHelper-scratch`. A cleanup that day deleted them, and the 11 tests on them skipped without a word. The labelled HP-bar clips went from `lab/recent`, which the rolling recorder prunes to its newest saves (`rolling.RECENT_KEEP_BYTES`: 20 GB today, 5 GB until 2026-10-29); `lab/lie_detector` is pruned the same way (`lie_recorder.prune`). So: sets live in `gamelab/lab/testdata/<set>` (git-ignored like the rest of the lab), a missing set is a failure, and `tests/test_testdata.py` fails if any test file names a scratch folder or one of the pruned lab folders.

**The sets.**

| Set | What | Labels (tests/fixtures) |
|---|---|---|
| `tree_dungeon_native` | 24 lossless 1366x768 frames of Tree Dungeon (map 10002073), saved 2026-10-28 19:17-19:19 on a crowded channel, 3 on each of platforms 13, 16, 18, 20, 21, 23, 25, 30 (`td_p<platform>_<i>.png`) | `tree_dungeon_native_monsters.json`: every monster (118), player and pet; no drops |
| `tree_dungeon_drops` | 7 frames of the 2026-10-24 hunts with drops lying (`hp0_*.png` from lab/shots) | `tree_dungeon_drops.json`: 45 drop sightings |

Lost and to be captured again: `tree_dungeon_clips`, 609 JPEG frames of her Tree Dungeon hunts of 2026-10-24/25 with labelled HP bars at 1366x768, pruned from lab/recent. The first map's `hp_bars_1920x1080` and West Rocky Mountain II's sets are no test's since 2026-10-31.

**Lookup.** `roots()` is `GAMELAB_TESTDATA` split on `os.pathsep` if set; otherwise `<repo>/gamelab/lab/testdata`, then the same folder in the main checkout when this checkout is a git worktree (a worktree's lab is a copy without the sets). `main_checkout()` reads the worktree's `.git` file (`gitdir: <main>/.git/worktrees/<name>`), follows git's `commondir` pointer to the shared `.git`, and returns its parent. `find(name, files)` returns the first root holding the set's folder with every named file.

**Failing loudly.** `folder(name, files, what)` returns the folder or calls `missing()` with every place it looked, each marked "(not there)" or "(without a.png, b.png, c.png ...)" (the first 3 missing files). `missing(why)` does `pytest.fail("TEST DATA MISSING: ...", pytrace=False)`, naming both environment variables, unless `GAMELAB_NO_TESTDATA` is set to anything but "" or "0", when it skips with "no test data (...)". `labelled(name)` reads the set's label file's `"frames"` and requires every frame it names. `lost(...)` is for a set whose frames are gone: its folder if they're back under the same names, else a skip saying "NEEDS A NEW CAPTURE" and how to make one (new labels too: the old ones fit only the lost frames).

**Who reads it.** test_bench, test_gates, test_loot, test_minimap_picture, test_perception (both sets, and `lost` for the HP-bar clips) and test_search_c. The `-rfEs` in pyproject.toml puts every such skip and its reason in the run's summary.

modules.title: The architecture rules
modules.tagline: Reads every gamelab import to keep the layers pointing downwards
modules.summary: A code-reading test: it parses every module under gamelab's layer packages and fails if one imports a layer above it. It also checks that the character profiles are data only, that the elevated key player loads none of the hunting stack, that only the perception service captures the game, and that no command has its own look flags.
modules.details_md:
**The rule.** gamelab is layered like a self-driving stack, and a layer imports only the layers below it plus the shared modules. `ALLOWED` is the whole policy:

| Layer | May import (besides itself and the shared modules) |
|---|---|
| perception | nothing |
| localization | perception |
| motion | localization |
| attack | perception, localization, motion |
| control | perception, localization, motion |
| behavior | perception, localization, motion, attack, control |
| ui | localization, motion, attack |
| analysis | perception, motion, control |
| sim | everything but ui |

`SHARED` are gamelab's top-level modules every layer may use: capture, character, classes, directions, gcstats, native, paths, screen, telemetry, window.

**How imports are read.** `gamelab_imports(path)` parses the file with `ast` and walks every node, so imports inside functions count too. A relative import is resolved against the file's own package (`from ..motion import x` in `gamelab/attack/` becomes `gamelab.motion`). A `from` import with nothing after the dots counts each imported name as a module (`from .. import paths, native` in `gamelab/attack/` gives `gamelab.paths` and `gamelab.native`). Only the second part of the dotted name is kept, which is the layer or shared module.

**The six tests.**

1. `test_layers_only_import_downwards`: one test per `.py` file under the nine layer packages (`LAYER_FILES`: 159 files on 2026-11-16), each asserting its imports minus `SHARED` and its own layer are within `ALLOWED`.
2. `test_every_module_belongs_to_a_layer`: every top-level `gamelab/*.py` except `__init__` and `__main__` must be in `SHARED`.
3. `test_her_profiles_are_data_only`: `character.py` and `classes/*.py` import nothing of gamelab but `paths`, `character` and `classes`, so any layer may read them.
4. `test_the_elevated_player_loads_only_what_it_needs`: a fresh Python imports `gamelab.__main__`, calls `build_parser()`, imports the player, the alarm and `perception.lie_detector`, and prints the loaded `gamelab*`, `gamedata*` and `tkinter*` modules. None may be from behavior, motion, localization, attack, ui, sim, gamedata or tkinter, and `gamelab.native` (it loads a DLL built from the tree) must not be loaded. The player runs as administrator and loads its code once, so it should carry as little as possible.
5. `test_only_the_perception_service_captures_the_game`: a plain text search of every gamelab file; `ScreenFrames(` may appear only in `localization/service.py` and `capture.shared()` only in `perception/frames.py`. One process holds the screen copy because a third DXGI duplication failed with 0x887A0022 when `watch`, the pet's babysitter and a hunt each held one (the test's docstring). The offline tools that time or read captures (bench-capture, bench-look --live) make their own `capture.Grabber` and don't trip it.
6. `test_no_command_looks_for_itself`: no subcommand of `build_parser()` has `--feed`, `--no-feed`, `--sweep` or `--no-sweep` (gone 2026-10-25: every look is the perception service's).

**What the rule forces elsewhere.** Control may not import attack, so the navigator asks behavior through a callback (docs/hunt-modes.md). Analysis may import neither localization nor sim, which is why the recordings' replay kit lives in `gamelab/sim` (README, Replaying the recordings).

the module list of a fresh Python process that imports the player's code path

failure messages naming the file and the layers it shouldn't import

decisions.what: gamelab split into layers like a self-driving stack; the import test and the elevated player's import test added.
decisions.why: The flat modules had grown (hunt.py alone was 1,276 lines); the player runs elevated and should load as little as before.

decisions.what: capture and native join SHARED; analysis may import motion; the elevated player must never load gamelab.native.
decisions.why: Screen capture became one shared grabber (gamelab/capture.py). The C pieces moved out of perception into the shared gamelab/native.py because motion may not import perception, and native loads a DLL built from the tree. analysis sits above control, which imports motion, and physics_check replays recordings through the movement engine.

decisions.what: Only the perception service captures the game; --feed/--sweep flags gone.
decisions.why: Every look is the service's; a third DXGI duplication failed with 0x887A0022 when several commands each held one.
gcstats.py was new and shared: Python's garbage collections counted and timed per reader, for the service and the commands that record (the writes-off-the-loops work).

decisions.what: character and classes checked to be data only.
decisions.why: Every layer may read her profile (localization's trackers take its Shape).

gotchas: Imports inside functions count: a lazy import can't dodge the rule.
The capture check is a plain substring search, so even a comment or docstring writing `ScreenFrames(` or `capture.shared()` in another file fails it.
motion may import only localization (not perception directly), and control may not import attack: the navigator reaches behavior through a callback.
analysis may not import localization or sim, so code that replays recordings through perception belongs in sim.
The elevated-player check runs in a subprocess, so it sees real import side effects, not this test process's already-loaded modules.

Only the nine layer packages are scanned. `gamelab/__main__.py` and the shared modules are not: `__main__` imports analysis, control and perception at the top and every other layer inside its command functions, which is why the subprocess test, not the import rule, keeps the elevated player lean.

flows.title: What happens when you type `python -m pytest`
flows.summary: How the suite is configured, spread over workers, trimmed of slow tests, and kept away from the game for every single test.
flows.trigger: A developer runs `python -m pytest` (or `--slow` before a commit).

steps.text: pytest imports conftest first. It sets GAMELAB_FIXED_STATS=1 and GAMELAB_NO_PUSH=1, drops GAMELAB_CHARACTER, and defaults OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS to 1 and GAMELAB_GPU to 0, all before any test imports gamelab.
pyproject's `-n auto` asks how many workers: 8 for the suite or a folder, 0 when only files or tests are named. `--dist worksteal` hands the long tests round as workers come free.
Without `--slow`, the items marked slow are deselected (64 of 3,818 on 2026-11-16).

Before each test: keys, window calls, DXGI and mss capture and paging refused; inbox, outbox, alarm and lab notes moved into the test's tmp_path; mutexes renamed per worker; locate.build reads only the test's own lab.
The last step of `offline`: open() and the os calls that change files refuse any path under gamelab/lab with SimViolation.
After the test, physics.reset() puts her walk and climb back to her profile's SPEED; monkeypatch undoes everything `offline` did.

At the end pytest's summary (`-rfEs` in pyproject.toml) lists every failure, error and skip with its reason: a test-data set missing (`TEST DATA MISSING`, or `no test data` under GAMELAB_NO_TESTDATA=1), a lost one (`NEEDS A NEW CAPTURE`), no game data copy.

flows.title: A test reads a labelled frame set
flows.summary: How a perception test gets Tree Dungeon's 24 labelled frames, and what happens when they aren't on this computer.
flows.trigger: A test such as test_minimap_picture calls `testdata.labelled(testdata.TREE_DUNGEON)`.

steps.text: The test asks for the set's labels and the path of every frame.
Reads tests/fixtures/tree_dungeon_native_monsters.json and takes its `frames` (24 names).
Asks for the set's folder with every one of those frame files in it, passing the set's description (`WHAT`) for the message.
Lists where to look: GAMELAB_TESTDATA's folders if set, else this checkout's gamelab/lab/testdata, then the main checkout's when this is a git worktree (main_checkout).
Returns the first root whose tree_dungeon_native folder holds all 24 frames.

If none does, `folder` walks the roots again to say what each lacked ("not there", or "without" its first 3 missing files) and calls `missing`: the test fails with "TEST DATA MISSING" and each place it looked, or skips if GAMELAB_NO_TESTDATA is set to anything but empty or 0.

flows.title: How the layer rules are enforced
flows.summary: test_architecture turns the README's layer diagram into one test per source file, plus a subprocess check of what the elevated player loads.
flows.trigger: Any pytest run (these tests are fast and always in).

steps.text: Collects every .py under the nine layer packages, one parametrized test each.
Parses the file and resolves every import, relative or absolute, to a gamelab layer or shared module.
Removes SHARED and the file's own layer; anything left must be in ALLOWED for that layer, or the test names the offending layers.
Starts a fresh Python that imports the command line, the player, the alarm and the Lie Detector spotter, then fails if any stack layer, gamedata, tkinter or gamelab.native got loaded.
Its subcommands are also checked for the old --feed/--sweep flags, which must stay gone.

flows.title: The simulator as a test bench
flows.summary: How the offline simulator's scenarios are checked inside pytest, and how that differs from the golden traces outside it.
flows.trigger: test_sim's scenario tests in a pytest run; `python -m gamelab.sim.golden check` by hand.

steps.text: One test per registered scenario (48 on Tree Dungeon), skipped without the map's game data; the 10 in `SLOW_SCENARIOS` (the tours end to end, those over 15 s, the key-following grinds) only with --slow.
Runs the scenario's real stack against the simulated world with a fake clock, a fake key player and fake eyes.
While it runs, time, the player client and every lab path point at fakes and a temp folder; anything reaching the game or writing under gamelab/lab raises SimViolation.
Lists what the scenario says it shows but the trace doesn't; the test asserts the list is empty.
Replays each nav_* scenario with Navigator.go written as begin/step (as the hunt loop drives it) and requires the same trace; 3 in the fast suite, the other 10 --slow.

Outside pytest: re-runs scenarios and compares each with its trace recorded in gamelab/lab/golden (git-ignored), part by part, every part but the scenario's `doc` (key plans, log, results, the world's summary); exit 1 on any difference, 2 when nothing could be run. tests/test_golden.py only checks that the --jobs pool gives the same bytes and output as one process.

not_done: The golden traces are not part of pytest: they are recorded and checked by hand (`python -m gamelab.sim.golden check --jobs N`) and live in gamelab/lab/golden, git-ignored, so a fresh checkout has none.
Real-map tests need the game data copy (gamedata/data, not in git): without it they skip with "needs Tree Dungeon's game data"; with it but broken they fail rather than skip (test_sim checks this).

Lost test data: `tree_dungeon_clips`, 609 frames of 1366x768 hunts with labelled HP bars, was pruned from lab/recent; its tests skip saying NEEDS A NEW CAPTURE until a hunt's frames are saved and labelled again.
The replay kit's tests on her recordings (golden-clips, 6.6 GB, outside git) skip without them.
test_no_hit_scenes keeps strict expected failures (`OPEN`) for scenes whose fault isn't fixed yet; each is meant to be flipped as its fix lands.

There is no CI configuration in the repository (no .github or other pipeline): the suite runs only when someone runs it. README.md asks for `python -m pytest --slow` (about 3 minutes) before a commit; gamelab/README.md's check order of 2026-10-28 asks for the fast suite.

The tests on the first map's (Thicket Around the Beach II) and West Rocky Mountain II's data went on 2026-10-31, with those maps' 90 simulator scenarios (the bot plays only Tree Dungeon). Their sets outside git (`hp_bars_1920x1080`, `west_rocky_native`, `west_rocky`) are no test's now; West Rocky's three frames kept in git (`tests/fixtures/native`) are still read by the 1366x768 tests (test_resolution, test_pasted and others).
